section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the independent variable, "Satisfaction with adult children's achievements," which was measured using a 5-point Likert scale across six areas. Participants rated their general satisfaction with adult children aged 25 or older, with the context implying a Nigerian setting based on references to Nigerian higher institutions. The measure achieved an internal consistency coefficient of .75 and fit the underlying construct.
section_summary.evidence_source: Independent variable Satisfaction with adult children's achievements. This was measured by asking participants to generally express their level of satisfaction with adult children's achievements in six areas namely education, occupation, health, finances, relationships and closeness to God using a 5-point Likert scale format which are as follows: very dissatisfied (0), dissatisfied (1), neither satisfied nor dissatisfied (2), satisfy (3) and very satisfied (4). Responses were based on the general satisfaction with the achievements of all adult children taken together and not just a particular adult child. Parents were asked to limit their ratings to adult children who have attained at least the age of 25. At this age, it is maximally possible (under normal circumstances) that an adult child would have attained a first degree education, have a job and developed mature relationships with the opposite sex whether marital or not. These assumptions were based on the evidence that the minimum age required for a child to gain admission into Nigerian higher institutions is 16 years (Lawal, 2018). Hence by age 20 (without any obstruction), adult children would have completed a first-degree education and ready to go into the world of work. An internal consistency coefficient of .75 was obtained for the measure of satisfaction with adult children's achievements. Also, present study data fits the underlying construct of satisfaction with adult children achievements, χ2 (5) = 9.21, p = .10, CF1 = .99, SRMR = .02, RMSEA = .043, and 90% CI = (.00, .085).
